title: Building the Blog Pages
description: Create the public blog list, post detail, and category pages using App Router, Prisma, and Static Generation with ISR.

slides.title: The Public Blog Faces 📄
slides.content:
# Three Main Pages

1. **Blog List** (`/posts`) – shows all published posts with title, excerpt, date.
2. **Post Detail** (`/posts/[slug]`) – full post content, author, comments.
3. **Homepage** (`/`) – featured posts, intro.

We'll build them as Server Components that directly query Prisma. No API routes needed for reading data!

slides.title: Blog List Page (app/posts/page.js)
slides.content: Fetch published posts, order by date, display titles and excerpts.

quizData.question: Why do we use `select` in the Prisma query instead of fetching all fields?

options.text: To reduce data transfer and only retrieve the needed columns
To hide the post content from users
Because Prisma doesn't support fetching all fields

quizData.explanation: `select` limits the columns returned, improving performance and security by not exposing unnecessary fields.

slides.title: Static Generation with ISR ⚡
slides.content:
# Making the Blog Fast

We want the post list and individual posts to be statically generated but stay fresh.

Add `revalidate` to the page level. In App Router, we can set `revalidate` in `fetch` options or use `export const revalidate = 60`.

Since we query Prisma directly, we'll use the page‑level export:

```js
export const revalidate = 60; // seconds
```

This tells Next.js to regenerate the page at most every 60 seconds when a request comes in (ISR).

slides.title: Post Detail Page (app/posts/[slug]/page.js)
slides.content: Dynamic route, fetches post by slug, shows full content.

quizData.question: What happens when a post is not found or not published?
quizData.explanation: `notFound()` from `next/navigation` will render the nearest `not-found.js` and set a 404 status.

slides.title: Pagination & Metadata 📇
Dynamic Metadata 🏷️
slides.content: For individual posts, use `generateMetadata` to fetch the post title and excerpt. This gives each page unique SEO tags.
